content.value_statement: AI teams need a clear path from idea to production. This skill organizes LLM apps, RAG systems, agents, ML pipelines, observability, and security into one workflow.
actual_capabilities: Breaks AI development into phases from product design through security review.
Lists specialist skills to invoke for LLM apps, RAG, agents, MLOps, and observability.
Provides copy-paste prompts for routing work to relevant AI and ML skills.
Includes checklists for API keys, rate limits, retrieval quality, agent roles, and monitoring.
Defines quality gates for testing, performance, security, observability, and documentation.
limitations: It is a coordination guide, not an implementation library or runnable tool.
It depends on separate referenced skills that may not be installed in every workspace.
It does not validate model choices, data quality, costs, or security controls automatically.
It does not provide complete project code or deployment scripts.

use_cases.title: Plan an LLM product build
use_cases.description: Use the workflow to define use cases, model choices, architecture, data flows, and success metrics before implementation.

use_cases.title: Coordinate RAG and agent engineering
use_cases.description: Use the phased skill list to route retrieval, vector database, agent architecture, and orchestration tasks to focused helpers.

use_cases.title: Prepare an AI system for production
use_cases.description: Use the observability, security, and quality checklists to verify monitoring, evaluation, access control, and documentation readiness.

prompt_templates.title: Start an AI project plan
prompt_templates.scenario: Beginner: define the basic direction for a new AI feature.
prompt_templates.prompt: Use this AI/ML workflow to plan a new AI feature. Identify the product goal, users, model needs, data flows, risks, and first implementation steps.

prompt_templates.title: Design a RAG system
prompt_templates.scenario: Intermediate: structure retrieval work for an internal knowledge assistant.
prompt_templates.prompt: Use this workflow to design a RAG system for my project. Cover ingestion, chunking, embeddings, vector storage, retrieval, reranking, caching, and evaluation.

prompt_templates.title: Build an agent workflow
prompt_templates.scenario: Intermediate: coordinate agent architecture and orchestration choices.
prompt_templates.prompt: Use this workflow to design an AI agent system. Define agent roles, tools, memory, orchestration, human review points, error handling, and test coverage.

prompt_templates.title: Prepare production AI gates
prompt_templates.prompt: Use this workflow to audit production readiness for an AI system. Check observability, security, evaluation, rate limits, access controls, cost tracking, and documentation.

output_examples.input: Plan a customer support AI assistant with retrieval over help center articles.
output: A phased plan covering product goals, model selection, RAG design, assistant behavior, evaluation, and rollout checks.
A list of specialist skills to invoke for prompt design, vector search, observability, and security review.
A readiness checklist for API key handling, rate limits, retrieval accuracy, tracing, alerts, and documentation.

output_examples.input: Review whether an internal AI agent platform is ready for launch.
output: A production readiness review across agent roles, tool access, memory, orchestration, human review, and error handling.
A security and observability checklist covering input validation, output filtering, abuse monitoring, tracing, and cost tracking.
A short list of gaps that must be resolved before launch.

best_practices: Start with product goals and success metrics before selecting models or frameworks.
Use the checklist to verify security, observability, and evaluation before release.
Install and review referenced specialist skills before relying on their prompts.
anti_patterns: Do not treat the workflow as production code or an automated deployment tool.
Do not skip security and observability phases when a prototype appears to work.
Do not invoke referenced skills without checking that they exist and match your project needs.

faq.question: What does this skill help me build?
faq.answer: It helps plan and coordinate LLM applications, RAG systems, AI agents, ML pipelines, observability, and AI security work.

faq.question: Does it generate complete application code?
faq.answer: No. It provides workflow structure, skill routing prompts, checklists, and quality gates for AI and ML projects.

faq.question: Can I use it with Claude, Codex, and Claude Code?
faq.answer: Yes. The report marks it as compatible with Claude, Codex, and Claude Code workflows.

faq.question: What should I install before using it?
faq.answer: Install or verify the referenced specialist skills that match your task, such as RAG, agents, MLOps, or evaluation skills.

faq.question: Does it handle security review?
faq.answer: It includes a security phase and checklist, but it does not replace a dedicated security audit.

faq.question: Who is the best user for this skill?
faq.answer: It is best for AI leads, engineers, and platform teams coordinating multi-step AI or machine learning projects.
